_about: Anís strategies (one per request type A1–H2, plus A7) and activities, as DATA. A strategy = small decision tree of shared tools, cheapest tier first, ending in 'choose format, then write'. Jev routes each message to a type; the agent (api/lib/assistant/agent.js) is the fallback. A strategy is switched on for its type only after it matches the agent on that type's tests. Test-question counts come from planning/anis-question-types-20261102.json (12,808 messages, a fast model's first-pass labels; test fixtures for measuring Jev's choices, never training data): lead = lead type, also = secondary type. A7 has no label in that file: counted by a request-for-original pattern (189 messages, mostly labelled A4/G3). Served by GET /api/v1/anis/{tools,strategies,activities} (api/lib/assistant/anis-docs-data.js + strategy-docs.js) and rendered on /docs/anis-tools, /docs/response-strategies (classes, composition, decisions) and /docs/anis-activities. Drafted 2026-11-03.

composition.intro: One message in four (3,343 of 12,808) needs more than one strategy, as do 34 of Immerse's 61; only 96 need three or more. Common sets repeat, so each becomes a combined strategy: independent strategies run in parallel, share what they find, and one writing step produces one answer.
rules: The lead sets the answer's shape; the others add steps to the plan, not separate answers.
Independent steps run in parallel; a premise check (E2) or name resolution (B5) runs first because the rest depends on it.
The writing model gets everything found and writes once, so nothing is said twice.
Each common set is logged and judged as its own strategy; a combination that keeps losing gets its own tree.

sets.example: “whats the bahai teaching on life after death, sources plz”
sets.how: One search serves both: B1's passages are quoted in full rather than paraphrased.

sets.example: “What does Islamic teaching say about Ikhlas?”
sets.how: The word study (original term, meaning) runs beside the teaching search; the answer opens with the meaning.

sets.example: “What does Buddhism say about homosexuality?” · “can christians believe in evolution”
sets.how: B1 with E3's rules: strict authority order, both the law and the guidance on treating people, no editorial.

sets.example: “What do Jewish scriptures teach about kosher dietary practices?” · “bahai funeral rites”
sets.how: Yes or no first, then the passage that says so in full.

sets.example: “Where does it say what dharma means? I want to read the explanation myself.”
sets.how: Search the term in its original and translated forms; one line of meaning above the passages.

sets.example: “Who is Ghoddus, and where in the texts is he mentioned?”
sets.how: Resolve the person first (which bearer of the name), then search passages about them.
Separate the teaching (why) from the rule (what), each cited.

sets.example: “Who wrote the Hidden Words? I have it down as Shoghi Effendi's work.”
sets.how: The false premise is checked first; the answer corrects it, then gives the real fact.

sets.set: A4 quotation + A5 reference / B2 explain
sets.example: “where does it say be generous in prosperity… I want to read the full context”
sets.how: Find the source (template), then read_around and, for B2, a short explanation below it.

sets.example: “Find where the scriptures of Islam and Judaism each talk about fasting, and how each one views it”
sets.how: The per-tradition searches double as the passage finder; each section quotes its own scripture.

sets.set: Follow-up move + the type it asks for
sets.example: “That passage you quoted is from 'Abdu'l-Bahá, not Bahá'u'lláh…”
sets.how: The move resolves what is meant from the thread; the type's strategy then runs, starting from the passages already found.

composition.note: Every example is a real test message from that set. Each count is one exact set of types (lead and others, any order).
moves_note: The same words can be either kind of message. “What about Islam?” after an answer on fasting is a comparison follow-up; as a first message it is a new question. “The second one” means nothing without the last reply. So every message is read together with its thread before it is classified.

In the conversation runs, 336 of the 393 turns that follow an earlier turn are follow-up moves, and 389 of the 412 turns need more than one strategy: the move, plus the strategy of what it asks for (a pushback that questions a citation runs E1 and A4; “which Hidden Word is that?” runs refer-back and A5). No test message asks for a reshape (“shorter”, “in Persian”, “email me this”), so the conversation runs must add them.

other_moves.must_do: Notice it and drop the old context.

other_moves.must_do: Give a good short answer and offer two directions. Ask a question only when no reasonable answer is possible.

activities_about: Activities are plugins on top of Anís: they inherit his character, voice and every tool and strategy, and add only their own steps, schedule, output and state. Jev's first decision on each message is none / search / activity; for an activity it also says start, continue, or step outside (a question mid-activity runs as a search; the activity resumes after). Channels: chat and email first; voice and tutorials later.

activities.name: Read a book with him
activities.start: Jev: activity · start ('help me read the Íqán', F6) · continue ('next', 'again', 'where was I') · step outside (a question about the paragraph → B2, then resume)
steps: find_work → the book's outline (sections, paragraphs)
send one page/section
notes on hard paragraphs (B2 strategy, author's own words)
ask what the reader makes of it; discuss the answer
remember the place
activities.schedule: Reader-paced in chat; email: one page per letter, next on reply or on the agreed rhythm

decisions.text: Jev is never trained. Each decision is made by giving Jev the information it needs, then adjusting that context until he decides right. The 12,808 labels are test fixtures for measuring his choices, nothing more.
Prepared knowledge means two things, both wanted: topic research collections (the free tier for A3, B1, B3, C3, D1, D3) and book research dossiers.
All three indexes will be built: prayers by occasion (D2), guidance by date with what supersedes what (D4), and the Bible / Qur'an / Gita reference parser (A5).

Every answer goes through a writing model, lookups included. The chosen format shapes the answer; the writer adapts the data to Anís's voice and the reader card and keeps answers varied. Lookups (A2, A4, A5, A7, D2, G3, H1) use a light writing model.
The light model runs without extended thinking and in its cheap price tier, for speed and cost.
